related_questions.question: Does Dipladenia come back every year?

text_blocks.snippet: Whether dipladenia comes back every year depends on the climate. In USDA Hardiness Zones 9 and above, dipladenia is a perennial and will return each year. In colder zones, it's typically treated as an annual or brought indoors for the winter. If you live in an area with frost, you'll need to bring your dipladenia indoors before the first frost to protect it and overwinter it as a houseplant.
snippet_highlighted_words: In USDA Hardiness Zones 9 and above, dipladenia is a perennial and will return each year

list.title: Perennial in Warm Climates:
list.snippet: Dipladenia is a perennial in warm climates (USDA Zones 9 and above) where it doesn't experience frost. In these areas, it can survive the winter outdoors and return the following year.

list.title: Treated as Annual in Colder Climates:
list.snippet: In colder climates (below USDA Zone 9), dipladenia is typically treated as an annual because it will not survive the winter outdoors. The first frost will likely kill it.

list.title: Overwintering:
list.snippet: If you live in a colder climate, you can overwinter your dipladenia indoors. Bring it inside before the first frost and place it in a bright, sunny location, like a south-facing window.

list.title: Dormancy:
list.snippet: During the winter, dipladenia will likely go dormant, meaning it will stop blooming and may drop some leaves. Reduce watering during this period, but don't let the soil dry out completely.

list.title: Re-planting Outdoors:
list.snippet: In the spring, once the danger of frost has passed (after May 10th in some areas), you can gradually acclimate your dipladenia back to the outdoors and resume normal watering and fertilizing.
